claim: In fiscal Q1 2019 (Oct-Dec 2018, iPhone XS/XS Max/XR quarter, the first quarter Apple stopped disclosing unit counts going forward), iPhone unit sales fell 11.5% YoY to 68.4 million despite three new premium models being launched.
stance_target: Prior 'supercycle' launch quarters can show unit declines even when new premium models are released, an early precedent for revenue growth decoupling from unit growth
scope_conditions: Apple fiscal Q1 2019, worldwide, Apple's own disclosed unit figure (last quarter before Apple stopped reporting units)
quoted_support: In fiscal Q1 2019 quarter, Apple shipped 68.4 million units of iPhones, worldwide. Despite launching three most expensive iPhones – iPhone XS Max, iPhone XS and iPhone XR – the company has registered a notable 11.5% YoY decline in its iPhone sales.

claim: Fiscal Q1 2017 (holiday quarter, pre-iPhone X, iPhone 7 era) was the historical peak for quarterly iPhone unit sales at that time: 78.29 million units, +4.7% YoY.
stance_target: Historical iPhone unit-sales peaks by fiscal quarter
scope_conditions: Apple fiscal Q1 2017 (Oct-Dec 2016), worldwide, Apple-disclosed unit figure
quoted_support: It was the fiscal Q1 2017 when the global sales of Apple iPhones reached an all-time high of 78.29 million units. That's 4.7% YoY and a whopping 72% QoQ growth.

claim: The iPhone 12 supercycle drove fiscal Q1 2021 (Dec quarter 2020) iPhone unit shipments to 90.1 million, +22.2% YoY, after a delayed-launch-driven unit decline of 10.6% YoY (41.6 million units) in the preceding fiscal Q4 2020.
stance_target: Comparison baseline for prior iPhone supercycle unit-growth magnitudes (iPhone 12, FY2021) versus the current iPhone 17 cycle
scope_conditions: Apple fiscal Q4 2020 and fiscal Q1 2021, worldwide, mix of Apple-disclosed and IDC-estimated figures (Apple had stopped disclosing units by this point, so these are IDC/analyst estimates cited by Dazeinfo)
quoted_support: Apple shipped a whopping 90.1 million units of iPhones during Oct-Dec 2020, worldwide. The 22.2% YoY growth was primarily driven by huge demand for the iPhone 12 series... The global iPhone sales declined a notable 10.6% YoY during the fiscal Q4 2020, totalling 41.6 million units.

claim: The iPhone X was the world's best-selling smartphone model in both fiscal Q1 2018 and fiscal Q2 2018, with 3 out of every 10 iPhones sold globally in fiscal Q2 2018 being an iPhone X, but no explicit total iPhone unit count for those quarters is given in this source.
scope_conditions: Apple fiscal Q1 2018 and fiscal Q2 2018, worldwide; qualitative claim only, no aggregate unit figure disclosed in this source
quoted_support: Despite tagged as 'failed' and 'flop', iPhone X emerged as the world's best-selling smartphone model in both, fiscal Q1 2018 and fiscal Q2 2018. In fiscal Q2 2018, 3 out of every 10 units of sold iPhones, globally, were iPhone X.
numbers: 30% of iPhone units sold in fiscal Q2 2018 were iPhone X
